translations.text: Simeon Peter, servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those to whom a faith of equal honour with ours has been allotted through the righteousness of our God and Saviour Jesus Christ.
Grace and peace be multiplied to you in the knowledge of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ!
He has granted us all the power of his own divinity for life and for the service of God through the knowledge of him who called us to his own glory and virtue.
Through these he has granted us very great and precious promises, so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature and may escape the corruption of the desire of this world.
And you too, applying this same diligence with all your effort, add virtue to your faith, and knowledge to your virtue,
and self-restraint (literally, fasting) to your knowledge, patience to your self-restraint, and godliness to your patience,
and brotherly love to your godliness, and love to your brotherly love.
When these things are with you and abound, you will be found neither idle nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
But whoever does not have these things is blind and cannot see, for he has forgotten that he was cleansed from his former sins.
Therefore, brothers, be all the more diligent to make your calling and election firm through good works, for if you do this you will never stumble at all.
Instead, in this way entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ will be richly provided for you.
For this reason I will not neglect to remind you of these things always, even though you know them and are firm in the truth that has come to you.
I have thought it right, as long as I am in this dwelling, to stir you up by reminding you.
I know that I am soon to leave this dwelling of mine, as our Lord Jesus Christ made known to me.
And I will be diligent so that, after my departure, each of you may be able to remember these things.
For we did not follow clever fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. Instead, we became eyewitnesses of his majesty.
For he received glory and honour from God the Father, when a voice came to him from such greatly magnificent glory: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
And we ourselves heard this voice come from heaven upon him when we were with him on the holy mountain.
And we have the prophetic word made more certain. You will do well to pay attention to it, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.
Know this first of all: no prophecy of scripture comes about by anyone's own interpretation.
For prophecy never came by the will of men. Instead, the holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit.

There were also false prophets among the people, just as there will also be false teachers among you. They will bring in destructive heresies and deny the Lord who set them free, and they will bring swift destruction upon themselves.
And many will follow their impurity, and because of them the way of truth will be blasphemed.
And with greed and with lying words they will make merchandise of you. Their judgment from of old does not rest, and their destruction does not sleep.
For if God did not spare the angels who sinned, but confined them in Tartarus with chains of darkness and handed them over to be kept for torment and judgment;
and if he did not spare the first world either, but preserved Noah, the eighth, a preacher of righteousness, and brought the flood of water upon the world of the ungodly;
and if he burned and overthrew the cities of the Sodomites and Gomorrahans, condemned them, and set them as an example for the ungodly who would come after;
and if he rescued righteous Lot, who was oppressed by the lawless who lived in filth
(for that righteous man, while he dwelt among them, was tormented in his righteous soul day after day by their lawless deeds, which he saw and heard),
then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, and the false ones they have kept under torment for the day of judgment.
This is especially true of those who follow in filth the track of the desire of the flesh and despise authority. Bold and self-willed, they do not tremble at the glorious ones, but blaspheme them,
whereas angels, who are greater in might and power, do not bring a blasphemous judgment against them from the Lord.
But these people, like dumb grazing beasts born by nature to be caught and destroyed, blaspheme what they do not understand, and they will perish in their own corruption.
And they will receive the wages of falsehood. They have reckoned [?] that desire as a day of pleasure. Defiled and filthy, they revel in their deceptions and feast together with you.
They have eyes full of adultery and of unceasing sin, and they lure unstable souls. They have hearts trained in greed. They are children of the curse.
They abandoned the straight way, went astray, and followed the way of Balaam son of Bosor, who loved the wages of falsehood.
He was rebuked for his own lawlessness by a dumb donkey, which spoke with a human voice and restrained the prophet's folly.
These people are waterless springs, clouds driven about by a storm, for whom the eternal gloom of darkness is reserved.
For with their exceedingly vain thinking they lure, through the desire of the flesh and filthiness, those who have truly escaped and those who live in error.
They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves of corruption, for people are enslaved to whatever overcomes them.

For if those who escaped the defilements of this world through the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ are entangled in them again and overcome, their last state has become worse for them than the first.
It would have been better for them not to have known the way of truth than to know it and turn back from the holy commandment that was given to them.
What has happened to them is what the true proverb says: "The dog has returned to its own vomit," and "The sow has washed only to wallow in the mire."
Behold, beloved, I am writing this second epistle to you. In these letters I stir up your minds with an eager reminder,
to remember the words spoken before by the holy prophets, and the commandments of the Lord and Saviour given through your apostles.
Know this first of all: in the last days scoffers will come, walking according to their own desires
and saying: "Where is the promise of his coming? For ever since the fathers fell asleep, everything has remained as it was from the beginning of creation."
For they deliberately forget this: that the heavens existed long ago, and the earth was formed out of water and through water by the word of God.
Through these the world of that time was flooded with water and perished.
But now the heavens and the earth are stored up by the same word, kept for fire until the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly people.
But do not forget this one thing, beloved: with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.
The Lord is not slow about his promise, as some consider slowness, but he is patient toward you, for he does not want anyone to perish, but wants all to come to repentance.
But the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night. On that day the heavens will pass away violently, the elements will burn up and melt, and the earth and the works in it will be burned up.
Since all these things are to be dissolved in this way, what sort of people ought you to be, in holy conduct and good service, as you wait
and hasten the coming of the day of God, on which the heavens will be set on fire and dissolved, and the burning elements will melt.
But according to his promise we wait for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.
Therefore, beloved, as you wait for these things, strive to be found by him spotless and blameless, in peace.
And regard the patience of our Lord as salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you according to the wisdom given to him,
as he speaks of this in all his letters. There are some things in them hard to understand, which the unlearned and unstable twist to their own destruction, as they also do the other scriptures.
You therefore, beloved, since you know this in advance, be on your guard, so that you are not carried away with the error of the lawless and fall from your own steadfastness.
But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and to the days of eternity. Amen.
